name: Punjab HEC International Travel Grant
amount: See website (economy airfare reported; confirm with PHEC)
eligibility: Faculty and non-teaching staff of provincially chartered public/private universities and public colleges in Punjab presenting a paper; at least one HEC-recognized journal publication in last 5 years; max 3 authors on the paper
eligibility_note: Restricted to staff of Punjab provincially chartered institutions; not open to federal-charter universities. Official page could not be fetched (HTTP 403); details from PHEC application forms hosted by universities.
how_to_apply_tip: Only useful if your employer is a Punjab provincially chartered university; max 2 grants per institution per conference, so coordinate with colleagues via ORIC.
deadline_quote: Official PHEC page (punjabhec.gov.pk/?p=165) returned HTTP 403 and could not be opened; no official deadline text verified.
verdict_reason: Official page blocked, so nothing could be verified. Search-index text of the PHEC page limits it to faculty of provincially chartered universities and public colleges of Punjab; BIC is a private college, not a chartered university, so this is very likely Not eligible.
eligibility_quote: (Unverified - search snippet of punjabhec.gov.pk/?p=165, page not opened) "Faculty members from provincially chartered public/private sector universities and public colleges of the Punjab."
ask_funder: Is a faculty member of a private transnational college in Punjab (Beaconhouse International College, delivering UK university degrees, not a provincially chartered university or public college) eligible for the PHEC International Travel Grant?

name: SIGPLAN PAC Travel Grants (incl. Long-Distance International Travel)
amount: Not fixed for long-distance grant; covers travel costs (airfare, lodging, registration); meals capped at USD 50/day in US, USD 60/day outside US
eligibility: SIGPLAN members presenting or serving on committees at SIGPLAN-sponsored events; long-distance grant for members living in Asia, Africa, Australia or South America; separate support for historically marginalized groups (no membership needed)
eligibility_note: Long-Distance International Travel grant explicitly targets members residing in Asia, Africa, Australia or South America - Pakistan (Asia) qualifies.
how_to_apply_tip: Submit at least 4 weeks before the conference's early-registration and early-hotel deadlines; funds are first-come first-served. Relevant if you publish ML-for-code / PL+AI work at PLDI, POPL, OOPSLA etc.
deadline_quote: "Travel requests for conferences are due at least four weeks before the early registration deadline and the early hotel reservation deadline of the conference."
verdict_reason: Long-Distance International Travel grant positively covers SIGPLAN members residing in Asia (Pakistan); no age, career-stage or institution restriction stated. Requires SIGPLAN membership and a SIGPLAN-sponsored event.
eligibility_quote: Long-distance international travel: "Applicants must be SIGPLAN members residing in Asia, Africa, Australia, or South America." Professional members: "Applicants must be SIGPLAN members and provide their ACM membership number."

name: Sindh HEC Research Travel Grant Program
amount: Registration fee (actual, max USD 1,000), accommodation USD 200/night (max 6 days), half daily allowance, travel cost as approved by SHEC
eligibility: Faculty of public and private universities (Sindh) presenting at internationally recognized conferences/seminars/symposia
eligibility_note: Provincial scheme for faculty of universities in Sindh
how_to_apply_tip: Download the SHEC travel grant form and policy from the page and apply well before travel; ask info@sindhhec.gov.pk about current ceilings.
deadline_quote: No deadline stated on the SHEC Travel Grants page or application form; applications are per event.
verdict_reason: The official application form restricts faculty eligibility to provincially chartered public/private universities; BIC is a private TNE college, not a chartered university (and the scheme is for Sindh institutions).
eligibility_quote: "a) VC /Pro-VCs/Rectors and Faculty members from provincially chartered public / private universities." (SHEC Application Form for International Travel Grant); page: grants are for "faculty members of Public/Private sector Universities, officers of SHEC and other relevant individuals."

name: IEEE SPS Conference Travel Grants (ICASSP / ICIP)
amount: Typically up to USD 750 (same region as conference) or up to USD 1,500 (other regions)
eligibility: Student and non-student authors with an accepted ICASSP/ICIP paper presented in person; active SPS membership; reference letter from supervisor/senior colleague
eligibility_note: Open to all countries; official page states applicants from developing countries receive higher priority.
how_to_apply_tip: Window is short (~10 days, e.g. 16-26 Jan 2026 for ICASSP 2026); join SPS (reduced developing-country fee) before applying and prepare the reference letter in advance for ICASSP 2027.
deadline_quote: Latest listed cycle: "Application Closed: 15 May 2026 at 23:59 (midnight) ET (Late Application will not be accepted)" (ICIP 2026). No ICASSP 2027 call posted yet.
verdict_reason: Grants are open to non-student authors in developing countries with priority for developing countries; no age, career-stage or institution restriction. Requires active SPS membership, accepted ICASSP/ICIP paper, in-person attendance and a reference letter.
eligibility_quote: Grants go to "student authors and non-student authors in developing and non-developing countries." "Higher priority will be given to eligible applicants from developing countries."

name: IJCAI Travel Grants (IJCAI Organization / AIJ)
funder: IJCAI Organization & Artificial Intelligence Journal Division
eligibility: Students, junior scientists and scientists attending IJCAI; priority to students and those with an accepted technical paper
eligibility_note: Official 2026 call lists no country restriction; applicants must state other sources of support and first seek departmental/local AI society funding.
how_to_apply_tip: Email the form with subject 'GRANT APPLICATION DOCUMENTATION'; include proof that HEC/institutional support was sought or insufficient.
deadline_quote: IJCAI-26: applications due "no later than June 4, 2026, midnight, AoE." No IJCAI-27 call found.
verdict_reason: Call covers "scientists" as well as students and junior scientists, with no country, age or institution restriction stated; priority goes to students and paper authors.
eligibility_quote: Grants are for "students, junior scientists and scientists" attending IJCAI-ECAI-26. Applicants "should first approach their department and/or local AI society for support before applying to IJCAI."

name: NeurIPS Financial Assistance
amount: Complimentary in-person or virtual registration and prepaid accommodation up to 7 nights (Atlanta, Sydney or Paris); flights, meals and per diem not reimbursed
eligibility: Anyone for whom attending is a financial burden; priority to students and junior postdocs who are primary contributors to accepted NeurIPS work
eligibility_note: No country restriction on official page; location-specific travel burden is a selection factor.
how_to_apply_tip: Only one application per person and you must be logged in to neurips.cc; pair it with HEC airfare since NeurIPS does not cover flights.
deadline_quote: NeurIPS 2026: "6 Oct 23:59 AoE" (applications closed); NeurIPS 2027 call not published.
verdict_reason: Program supports participation across all NeurIPS tracks with no nationality, age or career-stage exclusion; students/junior postdocs only get priority.
eligibility_quote: The program "supports participation across all NeurIPS 2026 tracks and programs." "Priority may be given to students and junior postdoctoral researchers"; applications "evaluated holistically based on accessibility needs, financial hardship, first-time attendance, service to NeurIPS."

name: Mediterranean Machine Learning (M2L) Summer School 2027 scholarships
funder: M2L School (with Google DeepMind and partners)
amount: See website (diversity scholarships; details not published)
eligibility: Doctoral and exceptional master's students, plus academics and practitioners worldwide; merit-based selection
eligibility_note: Open to applicants 'from around the world' with a Mediterranean focus; scholarship eligibility rules not yet published.
how_to_apply_tip: Call typically opens in early spring; ask for scholarship and request the visa letter early given Schengen processing times from Pakistan.
deadline_quote: M2L homepage states the school "will take place in Barcelona, Spain between August 30th and September 3rd"; no application deadline is published.
verdict_reason: Target audience is mainly doctoral/Master's students though academics worldwide are mentioned; scholarship eligibility rules are not published, so whether an Associate Professor from Pakistan can get a scholarship is unknown.
eligibility_quote: "The target audience consists primarily of Doctoral students or exceptional Master students." The school "actively encourage[s] and promote[s] diversity through scholarships and targeted outreach."
ask_funder: Are M2L 2027 scholarships (travel/accommodation) open to faculty (Associate Professor, PhD 2025) based in Pakistan, or only to students?

name: ICML Financial Aid
amount: In-person: registration + 7-night hotel; virtual: virtual registration (no travel support)
eligibility: Individuals for whom attending would be a financial burden; ICML account email must be linked to accepted paper(s)
eligibility_note: No nationality restriction on official page.
how_to_apply_tip: Incomplete answers lead to automatic rejection; link your OpenReview/ICML account to the accepted paper before applying.
deadline_quote: ICML 2026: applications closed on "18 May 2026 Aoe"; ICML 2027 page not yet published (404).
verdict_reason: Open to anyone for whom attending is a financial burden, with no country, age or career-stage restriction; requires an accepted ICML paper linked to the account.
eligibility_quote: Grants are "intended for individuals for whom attending the conference would cause a financial burden." "We are unable to provide travel support."

name: ICLR Financial Assistance
amount: Tiered (2026): registration+hotel (~USD 1,745) or reimbursement up to USD 1,500; hotel only (~USD 1,320) or reimbursement up to USD 1,000; registration only
eligibility: Students and early-career contributors (authors, workshop/tiny-paper authors, reviewers); considers financial hardship, cost of attendance, first ICLR
eligibility_note: No country restriction; priority to contributors from underrepresented demographic and geographic backgrounds.
how_to_apply_tip: ICLR 2027 paper decisions are 16 Dec 2026; watch iclr.cc for the FA form in Jan-Feb 2027 and choose the reimbursement tier if you need airfare.
deadline_quote: ICLR 2026: "March 1st, '26 (AoE)" (closed); ICLR 2027 financial assistance page not yet published (404).
verdict_reason: Aid targets "student and other early-career contributors"; 'early-career' is undefined, so it is unclear whether an Associate Professor with PhD <2 years qualifies. No country restriction (underrepresented regions prioritised).
eligibility_quote: Aim: "fund student and other early-career contributors"; priority to "student authors," "contributors from underrepresented demographic groups," and "contributors from underrepresented geographic regions."
ask_funder: Does ICLR financial assistance treat a faculty member (Associate Professor) who received the PhD in 2025 as an 'early-career contributor'?

name: ACM SIGWEB Fair Access Travel Grant
amount: Varies (e.g. USD 10,000 pool for CI 2026); covers registration, flights, accommodation and visa costs
eligibility: MSc/PhD students, postdocs and non-tenured professionals residing in ACM-listed developing countries; preference to presenting authors
eligibility_note: Requires residence in a country on ACM's Developing Countries Listing; ACM's lower-middle-income country list includes Pakistan. Offered per SIGWEB conference (TheWebConf, WSDM, HT, DocEng, CI/HCOMP, UMAP).
how_to_apply_tip: Explicitly includes postdocs; target WWW 2027 or WSDM 2027 and apply right after acceptance since pools run out.
deadline_quote: CI 2026: both travel grants closed and all funds awarded; no WSDM 2027 / WWW 2027 SIGWEB grant call posted yet.
verdict_reason: Grant is limited to students, postdocs or 'non-tenured professionals' resident in ACM-listed developing countries; an Associate Professor's tenure status is decisive and unstated, and the ACM listing page (403) could not be opened to confirm Pakistan.
eligibility_quote: "Open to all MSc and PhD students, post-doctoral researchers, or non-tenured professionals." Applicants must be residents of countries on the ACM Developing Countries Listing.
ask_funder: Does an Associate Professor on a non-tenure (contract) appointment at a private college in Pakistan count as a 'non-tenured professional', and is Pakistan on the ACM Developing Countries Listing?

name: ACL-family Diversity & Inclusion Subsidies (ACL, EMNLP, NAACL, EACL, AACL)
amount: Varies: travel + accommodation reimbursement, registration waiver, caregiving, bandwidth/VPN, ACL membership
eligibility: Students and researchers from underrepresented communities facing financial barriers; priority to authors and first-time attendees
eligibility_note: No country list; official call cites applicants from developing countries as an example; AACL-IJCNLP form explicitly targets 'researchers from developing countries'.
how_to_apply_tip: Reimbursement is post-conference with receipts, so book refundable tickets in case of visa denial.
deadline_quote: ACL 2026: applications due "May 15, 2026" (AoE); no 2027 ACL/EACL/NAACL D&I call found.
verdict_reason: Open to researchers facing financial barriers with no country, age or career-stage restriction; living in a developing country is given as a valid justification.
eligibility_quote: Encourages applications from "students and researchers from underrepresented communities facing financial barriers"; "Priority will be given to authors, first-time attendees and individuals from underrepresented communities"; example justification: "I live in a developing country".

name: IEEE RAS Member Support - Developing Country Travel Support (ICRA, IROS, CASE)
amount: Typically valued at USD 1,500; for ICRA 2027 given as prepaid hotel rooms by RAS with limited exceptions
eligibility: RAS members from developing countries (IEEE Developing Country Listing) with an accepted paper; also student members
eligibility_note: Explicitly for 'RAS members from developing countries, as defined by IEEE's Developing Country Listing'; Pakistan is a lower-middle-income country.
how_to_apply_tip: Relevant for robot learning / embodied AI papers; join RAS (developing-country dues) before applying.
deadline_quote: ICRA 2027 travel support page: application deadline "(Schedule TBD)". ICRA 2026 deadline was 25 Feb 2026.
verdict_reason: Non-student RAS members from IEEE-listed developing countries with accepted papers qualify; Pakistan is on IEEE's List of Developing Nations; no age/career/institution limit. Requires RAS membership and an accepted ICRA paper.
eligibility_quote: "Members of IEEE Robotics and Automation Society with accepted papers, from developing countries as determined by the" IEEE Developing Country Listing; IEEE 'List of Developing Nations' includes "Pakistan".

name: IEEE CIS Travel Grants - Developing Countries track (IJCNN, FUZZ-IEEE, CEC, SSCI, etc.)
amount: Typically USD 600 (intra-continental) or USD 1,200 (inter-continental), reimbursed after in-person attendance
eligibility: IEEE CIS members above student grade from developing countries presenting an accepted paper in person at a CIS-sponsored conference (separate student and industry early-career tracks)
eligibility_note: Dedicated 'Developing countries grant' for CIS members above student level; Pakistan is on IEEE's developing-country (World Bank lower-middle income) list. Official CIS page blocked automated fetch; details verified on IJCNN 2025 official grant page.
how_to_apply_tip: Become an IEEE CIS member before applying; only one travel grant per conference and you must declare any INNS/other grant applications.
deadline_quote: WCCI/IJCNN 2026: applications close "1st April 2026"; next CIS conference grant windows not yet posted. Main CIS page blocked (HTTP 418).
verdict_reason: The 'Researchers from Developing Countries' grant covers CIS members above student grade, but the opened conference page does not define which countries qualify and the main CIS travel-grant page could not be opened.
eligibility_quote: "IEEE CIS Conference Travel Grant for Researchers from Developing Countries" - for "IEEE CIS Members of any grade higher than Student."
ask_funder: Does the CIS 'Researchers from Developing Countries' grant use IEEE's developing-country listing (which includes Pakistan), and is a non-student CIS member at a private college in Pakistan eligible?

name: ISCA Travel Grants (Interspeech and ISCA workshops)
amount: Early registration and possibly accommodation; travel only in exceptional cases
eligibility: Students and early-career scientists with an accepted paper; no previous ISCA grant
eligibility_note: Official page: 'Applicants from all countries are eligible'; preference to applicants from areas needing greater support; low-income-country researchers may apply exceptionally.
how_to_apply_tip: Apply via services.isca-speech.org/iscagrants and do not register before the decision; submit report and receipts within 3 months.
deadline_quote: Apply "no later than the deadline specified on the website of the event." "If no deadline is specified, the application should be submitted no later than the early registration date of the event."
verdict_reason: Grants target students and early-career scientists ('early career' undefined); the low-income-country exception does not clearly cover Pakistan (lower-middle income). Nationality is fine.
eligibility_quote: "ISCA financially supports students and early career scientists"; "researchers in special situations like unemployment or coming from low income-level countries" may apply exceptionally; "Applicants from all countries are eligible."
ask_funder: Does ISCA consider a faculty member (Associate Professor) awarded the PhD in 2025 an 'early career scientist' eligible for an ISCA travel grant?

name: ICTP Schools & Workshops participant grants (incl. ML/AI activities)
funder: Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP)
amount: No registration fee; limited grants covering travel and/or local living costs
eligibility: Early-career researchers and PhD students; priority to participants from developing countries
eligibility_note: ICTP event pages state grants are available 'with priority given to participants from developing countries'; Pakistan is a developing country under ICTP rules. 2027 calendar (72 activities) includes AI events e.g. 'School and Workshop on AI for Emulation, Hybrid and Surrogate Modeling in Science' and 'Rethinking AI: Frugal Intelligence for Global Good Workshop'.
how_to_apply_tip: Apply via the event's Indico 'Apply here' link and tick the financial support box; the deadline for those requesting funding/visa is earlier than the general one (e.g. 30 Apr vs 12 May for a July 2026 ML school).
deadline_quote: ICTP news: "ICTP charges no fees for its events, and provides some financial assistance to participants from developing countries." Deadlines are set per event on Indico; the AI school pages opened show no deadline (e.g. 'School and Workshop on AI for Emulation...' 18-25 Jun 2027, listed 'Application Closed'/not yet open).
verdict_reason: ICTP gives some support to developing-country participants, but eligibility (career stage, region) is set per event and the 2027 AI events have not published criteria; some (e.g. Kuwait workshop) are region-limited.
eligibility_quote: "ICTP charges no fees for its events, and provides some financial assistance to participants from developing countries."
ask_funder: For the 2027 'School and Workshop on AI for Emulation, Hybrid and Surrogate Modeling' (smr 4362) and 'Rethinking AI' workshop (smr 4366), are faculty (Associate Professor, PhD 2025) from Pakistan eligible for travel/living grants, and what is the application deadline?
